name: chronoflow
description: Todo app and time tracker with Jira integration

scripts.dev: concurrently -k --handle-input -n main,renderer "npm run dev:main" "npm run dev:renderer"
scripts.build: npm run build:main && npm run build:renderer

releaseInfo.releaseNotes:
### ChronoFlow v0.1.16

#### New Features:
- **Dev fully isolated from production data:** dev builds use their own userData folder + database, can never touch the production DB, and show a DEV badge in the title bar (dev and the installed app can run side by side).
- **Play-button styling & tracking indicator on dashboard entries:** same filled play button as the issues view on every entry, with a pulsing dot + row highlight on the entry currently being tracked.
- **Running timer survives an app restart:** an open timer is restored on startup and keeps counting from its original start time.
- **Resume an open entry from the dashboard:** open (endless) entries have a play button that resumes timing from the entry's original start time.
- **Split improvements:** you can now start a split block at the entry's exact start time (e.g. remove/move the first hour after a lunch break), and when moving a block/part to another issue the comment is shown in an editable field (defaults to the original comment) instead of being copied blindly.
- **No seconds when manually editing times:** start/end time fields are minute-accurate (HH:MM) instead of showing seconds.

#### Fixes:
- **Data-loss root cause fixed:** issue/project syncs no longer wipe time entries (`INSERT OR REPLACE` → upsert) — previously the `ON DELETE CASCADE` could silently delete entries on every sync/load.
- **Worklog loading uses local day boundaries:** night worklogs (00:00–02:00 local) no longer get missed on both days.
- **Null-note crash fixed:** editing a time entry with an empty comment no longer crashes the save.

#### Notes:
- Pause state is not persisted: quitting while paused resumes as running on next start.
